hlni.insight: Degree titles do not define the specific daily work or feedback loops; an audit of coursework components does.
hlni.audienceGap: Students assume degree names imply a specific, uniform experience.
hlni.viewerChange: Moves from passive comparison of labels to active, precise questioning of curriculum delivery.
hlni.support: The method relies on separating production, evaluation criteria, and feedback, which are independent of the degree name.
hlni.payoff: The audit reveals missing information, forcing the student to ask a concrete, actionable question.

reelTitle: B.Com vs BBA: The Coursework Audit
creativeAngle: Trust-based methodology for evaluating academic requirements
objective: Replace degree-name anxiety with a structured, data-driven comparison method.
targetAudience: +2 students seeking academic depth and well-supported course and career decisions

shots.name: The Blank Audit
shots.visual: A student looks at two folders labeled B.Com and BBA. They pull out a blank grid titled 'Coursework Audit'.
shots.dialogue: Stuck between B.Com and BBA? Stop guessing based on titles.
shots.cameraPerformance: Close-up on the student's face, then pan to the grid.

shots.name: Filling the Grid
shots.visual: The student writes in three columns: Work Product, Assessment Criterion, Feedback Type. Many boxes remain empty.
shots.dialogue: Use this audit. Map out the work product, assessment criteria, and available feedback. If the boxes are empty, you lack data.
shots.cameraPerformance: Top-down view of pen filling the table.

shots.name: The Precise Question
shots.visual: The student points to a blank cell and writes a specific question in the margin.
shots.dialogue: Ask: What specific type of feedback is provided on the practical assignments in this module?
shots.onscreenText: What specific type of feedback is provided on the practical assignments in this module?
shots.cameraPerformance: Macro shot of the question being written.

productionNotes.editing: Rhythmic cuts matched to writing actions.
productionNotes.sound: Minimal ambient room tone, clear voiceover.
productionNotes.casting: A student in a neutral, studious environment.

creativeSummary.keyCreativeIdea: Shifting from vague degree comparison to evaluating specific academic deliverables using a structured audit.

selected.title: The Coursework Audit
selected.audienceGap: Belief that degree titles define the exact daily workload and assessment methods.
selected.hlni: A task label alone does not tell you what you must produce, what will be assessed, or what feedback you receive. Ask these as separate questions.
selected.viewerChange: Replaces vague degree-choice anxiety with a structured method to evaluate specific course requirements.
selected.concept: A student compares two blank 'Coursework Audit' worksheets to realize they need more data than just the degree name.
selected.device: Split-screen view of two worksheets where the student fills in columns for 'Work Product,' 'Criterion,' and 'Available Feedback.'
selected.support: The method separates three different pieces of information; it does not assume particular course content.
methodSteps: Ask what criterion is used to assess it.
Ask what feedback is available; mark unknown answers as questions.
selected.interpretationRule: Use the unanswered cells to ask a precise question about the actual course or task before deciding.
selected.visibleProof: A three-column question sheet turns one vague preference into a concrete unanswered question.
selected.payoff: Use the unanswered cells to ask a precise question about the actual course or task before deciding.
selected.limitations: This is a question-forming aid, not a degree ranking, aptitude test or prediction of success.

demonstration.input: A three-column grid: Work Product, Assessment Criterion, Feedback Type.
demonstration.observation: Several cells remain blank because generic course descriptions don't provide this specific detail.
demonstration.nextQuestion: What specific type of feedback is provided on the practical assignments in this module?

comparedWith.hlni: A short illustrative activity can reveal where you need help or what you want to investigate next; it cannot determine which degree suits you.
comparedWith.device: A physical journal entry shown on camera capturing a specific hurdle during a sample exercise.

comparedWith.hlni: The same total can result from different component values; an aggregate alone cannot tell you the underlying mix.
comparedWith.device: Animated bar charts that 'deconstruct' into different sub-components.

conceptSelection.contrast: The selected mechanisms provide distinct ways to handle uncertainty: 'Trust' focuses on auditing workload (Assessment Audit), 'Connection' focuses on identifying personal research gaps (Task Journaling), and 'Discovery' focuses on mathematically demonstrating why labels are often misleading (Aggregate Counterexample).
